headline: Am I still allowed to want a soulmate?
note:
FRAME: soulmate x age band. NO MAN EXISTS YET — she asks WHEN or WHETHER. Must not fall through to decode-him.
🔴 THE AGE BAND LIVES IN THE AD SET, NEVER IN THE COPY. No age, no number, no life-stage.
🔴 NO DURATION, forward or back — 'not much longer' is a LENGTH, and a length is not a date.
⚠ SHE is the subject of beats 3-6; the male figure is described in beats 1-2 and retired there.
⚠ NO FAMILY-LINE LANGUAGE anywhere in the read.

🔴 A PERMISSION QUESTION, AND THE READ MUST NEVER RULE AGAINST HER. It also must not grant permission as though it were Evelyn's to give — the answer is that nobody hands that out. No shame anywhere in the read.
⛔ 'the wanting' is banned by check-draft as a verb turned into a noun; every line here says 'to want' instead.

readback.1 would a person say this: Yes. 'And you've kept it to yourself' is a feeling that reaches, not a fact that can miss.
readback.2 is every noun real: The self-laid table, the unjudged face, the already-taken step — all on the card.
readback.3 anything she could catch me getting wr: No. Beat 4 says nobody has come and that she is asking whether she may. The ad is that question.
readback.4 does the symbol prove the line at a gl: Yes. A man who set his own table out and asked nobody proves 'you need no one's say-so'.

a: You turned the Magician. You reached without seeing, and your hand landed on the busiest card here.
Look at his hands. One is raised, the other points down, and both are working.
You asked if you're still allowed to want a soulmate. What catches me is that neither hand is empty.
Still, nobody has come. And you've started asking whether you're allowed to want it.
Whatever is in the way of this holds steady. I don't think any of it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's got hold of it…
b: You turned the Hanged Man. Nothing told the three apart, and you took the calmest man in the deck.
He hangs upside down by one ankle. Look at his face, though — it's calm.
You asked if you're still allowed to want a soulmate. It's the pause itself I keep looking at.
And yet nobody has come. And the question has turned into whether you may even ask it.
Something is sitting between you and this, close in. I don't think it began with you.
Let me look closer at what's sitting there…
c: You turned the Fool. Face down, all three, and you took the one in full sun.
Look at the sky behind him. It's gold, and there isn't a cloud in it.
You asked if you're still allowed to want a soulmate. The sky is gold and his foot is already moving — that's what I'm looking at.
But nobody has come. And you're the one asking whether it's alright to hope.
Something turns up as soon as this gets going. I don't think this began with you.
Let me look closer at what that is…
